Uncropped, as a photograph it would rate about 7.8, but it is not scored because it fails. It has the crispest braid in the camp so far, the hoop spans about 12% of the frame width, and the light is soft and warm. Against that, the frame is mostly black hair and cheek, the face is half-present, and the top reads white rather than ivory.
fix: Reshoot from behind, as W06_a3 was (that plate passed): the camera straight behind her, or at most about 20 deg to the side, with the head facing directly away so the cheek, jaw and nose are hidden by the head and neck. In frame: the back of the head (the neat low bun from the original W09 frame, or loose hair falling down her back, never forward over the face), the ear seen from behind, the hoop, the nape, the neck and the warm-ivory work-shirt collar or kurta at the bottom. Leave at least 150 px of neck, hair or wall beyond the hoop on the face side. Do not use a hair curtain over the face: in this attempt the model left the cheek bare in front of the curtain and the profile showed through it. Keep the blush wall, the crisp braid, the polished disc under the latch end and the hoop at about 40-45% of the ear's height. Make the garment warm ivory, not white.
